howDoI.q: How do I make a monster walk a path?
How do I make a monster that hurts when touched?
How do I make a monster my hero can pop?
How do I make a monster that can only be reached from above?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Meet the Monsters is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a couple of minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

pages.head: Level 1: Walk and Hurt
pages.html:
Level 1: Walk and Hurt

The MONSTERS WALK A PATH sign stands before a purple gumdrop that waddles four blocks to the right, turns, and waddles back, again and again. The JUMP OVER IT sign says what to do about it. Further on, the TOUCHING HURTS sign stands before a snail that creeps along slowly. The gumdrop is friendly: it bumps nothing and costs you nothing, so you can meet it safely. The snail is the one that hurts: touching it takes 10 of your 50 hit points once, and it goes dazed and flickers for about three seconds, when it cannot hurt you again. It takes five separate bumps to lose a life. Watch the gumdrop turn, then jump when the way is clear. The EXIT → sign points to the way out.

Coins are worth ten points each. There are eight, and some of them float where only a jump reaches.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The path. Open meet.mon in the monsters editor and pick the gumdrop. Its path is a short list of corners: it starts where you put it on the map, walks four blocks right at speed 2, then walks back facing the other way. The snail is the same idea, two blocks at speed 1. Change a corner or a Speed and play again.
  • Where it starts. In the map editor, one.map has a monster layer. A monster stands on the block you placed it on, and its path is measured from there.
  • Touching hurts. The hurt is not in the monster file. It is in the monster's picture: open meet.mbl in the blocks editor and look at gumdrop0. Its Hit points is −10. The engine adds that to the hero on every tick the picture overlaps her, not once per touch, so a monster that only hurts would take everything in a second. The snail does something about it. Its Power in meet.mon is 1, and a monster below 100 changes the moment it touches the hero into the monster named in When destroyed it becomes: a dazed snail. That one flickers, its picture has no hit points, and its Lifetime of 54 ticks (about three seconds) ends by turning it back into the snail. One touch, one hurt. Its picture is not solid, so nothing holds you inside it while it hurts. The gumdrop's picture has 0 hit points: it only walks its path.
  • You see it. The hero's Hurt sequence plays, with its sound, each time her hit points drop.
  • Hit points and lives. Open hero.chr in the character editor. The hero starts with 50 hit points and 3 lives. At zero hit points she falls over, a life is spent, and the level starts again. With no lives left the game ends.
  • The signs. Each sign is a few ordinary blocks side by side, with the words drawn in their pictures. Change the words in the blocks editor and play again.
  • The exit. A scene link joins the door at the end to the next level. Open meet.gam in the scenes editor and look at the links of the Walk and Hurt scene.

pages.head: Level 2: Pop and Lives
pages.html:
Level 2: Pop and Lives

The LAND ON TOP TO POP IT sign stands beside a pit, and at the bottom of it sit two mint green gumdrops. Drop in and land on them: each pops with a short sound and is gone, and you get 50 points. Then jump out. Further on, the WATCH YOUR LIVES sign warns of a purple gumdrop that does hurt, a little, the same way the snail does. Press F2 at any time to see your lives and hit points; the game has no counter on the play screen of its own. A second pit with two more mint gumdrops comes before the exit.

There are eight coins, and four monsters to pop.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • A monster that can be popped. The mint gumdrop's Power in meet.mon is 1. A monster below 100 is destroyed when it touches the hero. Nothing is named in When destroyed it becomes, so it is simply gone. Its picture, pop0 in meet.mbl, gives 50 Score points and no hit points, so it is harmless.
  • Why a pit, and not a stomp. Game-Maker cannot tell which side of a monster you touched. Any touch with Power under 100 pops it, from above, from the side or from below, so there is no landing-on-top rule to switch on. The level is built so that you can only reach the gumdrops from above: a pit with a monster at the bottom, and you fall onto it. Say so on the sign, as here: the pit is the trick, not a rule the game checks.
  • The pit. Open two.map in the map editor. The pit is two blocks wide and two deep, cut out of the grass and dirt, with the monsters placed in the bottom row. It is shallow enough for one jump to climb out.
  • Lives. The hero starts with 3 lives in hero.chr. Lose all the hit points and one is spent. F2 is Game-Maker's own status page, so it works in any game.
  • The exit. The last door links to the The End scene in meet.gam, which plays the ending.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Make the gumdrop's path longer, or its Speed faster.
  • Change the Hit points of the snail's picture so it hurts more, or not at all.
  • Lengthen the dazed snail's Lifetime so it stays harmless longer.
  • Make a monster that turns into a coin when it pops: add a monster that is a coin picture, and name it in When destroyed it becomes.
  • Give the hero 5 lives in hero.chr.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
